Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The players and umpires return to the park. The usual opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma stride out to open for India Women. It will be Ayabonga Khaka, to begin with the ball for South African women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, India Women need 190 to start the T20I series on a winning note. Can they do it or will South Africa Women get their first win of the tour? We shall find out soon. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Tazmin Brits is in for a chat. She says that she is glad to help the team get to this total. Tells that she swung too hard at the start instead of holding her base. Feels that the wicket is not too bad and this is a good score. Backs her bowlers to defend the total.

The Indian Women bowlers bowled a few tidy overs at the start but were taken to the cleaners through the middle and the fag end of the innings. Pooja Vastrakar was the pick of the bowlers with 2 for 23 in her spell while Radha Yadav accounted for a couple as well but was on the expensive side. The other spinners, Asha Sobhana and Deepti Sharma also went for plenty on this belter of a pitch. India Women batters will have their work cut out in the chase.

An outstanding batting effort from the Proteas Women powers them to a massive score of 189 for 4 in their 20 overs. Having sent into bat first, the skipper Laura Wolvaardt got them off to a fast start where Tazmin Brits was struggling at the other end. Wolvaardt departed for a quick fire 33 in the 8th over when Marizanne Kapp joined Brits in the middle. The duo took their time initially but settled in nicely and added 96 for the second wicket. Kapp smashed a brilliant 57 off 33 while Tazmin Brits departed on the final ball for the innings for a well-made 81. South African Women have posted the runs on the board and will be confident of defending it, going into the break.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tazmin Brits holes out on the last ball. Much fuller by Pooja Vastrakar, outside off, Tazmin Brits moves to the leg side nice and early and tries to cross bat this one down the ground. Fails to get the elevation and ends up hitting it flat and straight down the throat of long on where Radha Yadav reverse cups it. 6 runs and a couple of wickets off the last over. South Africa Women end with 189 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks are on the field now! South African women are off to a pretty good start and are going at nearly 8 runs to the over at the halfway mark of their innings. Their skipper Laura Wolvaardt gave them a fast start but was dismissed around her legs. Marizanne Kapp and Tazmin Brits have started to find their feet and are doing fairly well. The Proteas Women will look to post over 175 from hereon. India Women, on the other hand, have been decent but have bowled a few loose balls. They will need to pick a few wickets and stem the flow of runs. Asha Sobhana (1-0-6-0) returns to the attack.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the national anthems and we are all set to go. The two umpires make their way out to the middle. A huge roar from the crowd greets Harmanpreet Kaur and her troops as they disperse from the huddle to take their respective field positions. It will be Tazmin Brits and Laura Wolvaardt to open the innings for South Africa Women. Renuka Singh has the new ball in hand and she is raring to go. She is starting with a slip in place. Let's play...

The first ball in the series opener is moments away, but before that, Harmanpreet Kaur and Laura Wolvaardt will lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa first, followed by that of India.

The captain of South Africa Women, Laura Wolvaardt says that they would have bowled first as well. Tells that they will assess what the wicket does and try to put a good score on the board. Shares that T20I has not been a great format for them as a team in the recent past, but this is a wonderful opportunity for them to tweak a couple of things before the T20 World Cup. Informs that Chloe Tryon is back in the mix.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they want to have a total on the board which will give them an idea of how to go about it. Adds that they are going with a similar mindset as they did in the Bangladesh series and they have an eye on the T20 World Cup later in the year. Ends by sharing that they are going with the similar XI that played the first ODI.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Marizanne Kapp, Anneke Bosch, Chloe Tryon, Nadine de Klerk, Annerie Dercksen, Eliz-Mari Marx, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Nonkululeko Mlaba, Ayabonga Khaka.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Dayalan Hemalatha, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Asha Sobhana, Renuka Singh.
TOSS - India Women have won the toss and they have opted to BOWL first.

On the flip side, South Africa after facing defeats in the Test and the ODI leg of the tour will hope to put in a much-improved show in the shortest format of the game. South Africa are going with a similar squad as they had for the ODI but have added Chloe Tryon to the mix. The experienced all-rounder will lend a balance to the side and will play a pivotal role in finishing the innings. Marizanne Kapp is not fully fit to resume bowling but her batting will be key for her side. Laura Wolvaardt and Sune Luus had a decent run in the only Test and will want to continue the form while Nadine de Klerk, Masabata Klaas, and Nonkululeko Mlaba will be the other key players for the South Africa Women. Laura Wolvaardt will hope to find a balanced XI in this series with an eye on the T20 World Cup looming in another three months’ time. Can South Africa Women get their first win of the tour or will the Women in Blue carry on the winning momentum? Let’s find out. Toss and team news coming shortly.

Hello and warm welcome to our coverage of the 1st T20I in the 3-match series between South Africa and India Women at the M.A Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. India Women have been ruthless so far and won all the games in the series. They swept the ODI series 3-0 and won the only Test quite convincingly. Most of the team is in good form and the Harmanpreet Kaur-led side will want to carry on the unbeaten run. The likes of Amanjot Kaur and Sajeevan Sajana are the fresh additions to the T20I squad while Shabnam Shakil and Uma Chetry are the ones to keep an eye on for the future. India Women will look to experiment with their side and find a perfect combination before they head into the Women’s Asia Cup later in the month.
